disclaimer.title: Important clinical notice
disclaimer.body: CETUS is a complementary tool to support therapy, used under professional supervision. It is NOT a standalone treatment and does not replace clinical care. Cue exposure can provoke intense craving. Use only under professional supervision and with a safety plan. You can stop the session at any time with the STOP button.

uscs.title: Urge-specific coping skills
uscs.intro: Work through these steps to manage the urge. Each step is an evidence-based skill.
uscs.name_feeling.title: Name what you feel
uscs.name_feeling.prompt: What emotion and physical sensation do you notice right now? Describe them in your own words.
uscs.recall_negative.title: Recall a negative consequence
uscs.recall_negative.prompt: Think of something using has cost you. What did you lose or what harm did it cause?
uscs.recall_benefit.title: Recall a benefit of not using
uscs.recall_benefit.prompt: What do you gain by staying substance-free? Something that matters to you today.
uscs.alternative_action.title: Choose an alternative action
uscs.alternative_action.prompt: What can you do instead right now? A concrete, doable action.

gallery.empty: Add images to the media/positive folder or mark them as a reason for recovery.
calm.title: You are safe. Breathe.
calm.body: The session has stopped. Take a moment. Breathe in slowly… hold… breathe out slowly.

settings.autoscroll_hint: Advance to the next cue automatically. Off by default.
settings.autoscroll_on_grading: Advance after each craving rating (periodic or peak)
settings.accessibility_hint: Drive the exposure with an adaptive keyboard (Enter, +, −, arrows, 0–9). Full detail in Help. Applies on the next session.

settings.shared_note: Shared with all users of this clinic.
settings.advanced_hint: Extra craving measurements, beyond the fixed periodic interval. Both off by default.
settings.vas_every_n_cues: Measure craving every N cues (0 = disabled)
settings.adaptive_ordering_hint: CETUS learns from the ratings which cues provoke more craving for each patient and suggests a low→high order. The clinician reviews and applies it in the cue library; it never changes a live session.
settings.vas_per_cue_seconds: Measure craving after N seconds on the same cue (0 = disabled)
settings.progressive_hint: Gradually applies a down-regulation lever over the session duration. The progressive value acts as a floor: the patient can increase it but not decrease below it.
settings.auto_coping_enabled: Open coping automatically on consecutive high scores
settings.session_options_hint: Defaults; adjustable per session with the Parameters button.

wizard.title: Patient Setup Wizard
wizard.mode_intense_reason: For patients with sustained abstinence, intense graded exposure maximizes extinction learning per session [1][2]. CET with USCS produced fewer heavy drinking days at 6 and 12 months [2].
wizard.mode_interspersed_reason: Interspersed neutral stimuli moderate exposure intensity, reducing risk of overwhelming craving [3][6]. Validated neutral control images are matched for visual properties [10][11]. The E-Reva protocol incorporates neutral environments [8].
wizard.vas_recommendation: VAS is the gold standard for craving measurement in CET [9]. 30-second intervals provide good temporal resolution for habituation tracking [4][5].
wizard.habituation_recommendation: Within-session habituation criterion: two consecutive ratings ≤ 2/10. Based on Powell et al. (1993) [3] — each exposure continues until habituation occurs.
wizard.coping_recommendation: USCS teaches four evidence-based coping skills [1][2]. Auto-coping triggers at 3 consecutive ratings ≥ 7/10 to ensure practice at peak craving moments.
wizard.cue_recommendation: CET protocols typically use 8–20 cues in graded order [1][4]. The Mellentin app used 8 alcohol videos [4]. MOCIS provides 120 images per substance [11].
wizard.apply_defaults: Apply as defaults for this patient
wizard.first_time: This is the first session for this patient. The setup wizard will help configure optimal parameters based on clinical evidence.
wizard.no_cues_warning: No cues are assigned to this patient. Configure cues before starting a session.
wizard.interspersed_evidence: Standard cue-reactivity paradigms use 5–10% craving cues among neutrals. Clinical exposure typically uses fewer craving cues than research protocols.
wizard.dynamic_evidence: When craving remains elevated, extending neutral cue runs provides a natural cooling-off period before the next craving cue.
import.welcome_subtitle: This wizard helps you download cue images for exposure sessions.
import.welcome_body:
CETUS needs images to run exposure sessions:

• Neutral images: everyday objects that do not evoke craving (used in Interspersed mode)
• Substance cues: images related to the target substance

This wizard will guide you through downloading both types.
import.pexels_subtitle: To search and download images, you need a free API key from Pexels.
import.pexels_step1: 1. Visit the Pexels API page and create a free account
import.pexels_step2: 2. Copy your API key from the dashboard
import.pexels_step3: 3. Paste it below and click Verify
import.gemini_subtitle: For smart tag suggestions on neutral images. You can skip this step.
import.neutral_subtitle: Neutral images are non-craving control stimuli for the Interspersed Neutral session mode.
import.neutral_explain: Search for everyday objects, office supplies, kitchen items, or landscapes — anything that does not evoke craving.
import.substance_subtitle: You can also download craving-inducing images. This step is optional.
import.substance_tips:
Tips for good cue images:
• Clear depiction of the substance or paraphernalia
• Consistent lighting and background
• Avoid images with identifiable faces
• Multiple angles and contexts increase variety
import.dedup_subtitle: Scan all media folders for duplicate images by content (SHA-256).
import.dedup_periodic: {n} duplicate file(s) found in your media library. Would you like to review them now?
import.summary_body: You can always import more images from the cue library (🌐 Import from Web button) or Settings → Media Tools.
